description: Shared defaults for my app repos (autopakr, pakr, ynab, fastmail, fastmail-mcp). Weekly and grouped. mise.lock moves with mise.toml (Renovate's mise manager rewrites it in the same PR), so each batch runs CI once. Patches merge themselves once CI passes (a repo without PR checks never automerges: Renovate waits for a green status); minors and majors wait for review. homelab has its own config. Toolchain rules match dep names: the package name of a Docker image or a mise tool is often not the bare tool name.

customManagers.description: Versions pinned in workflows with a '# renovate: datasource=… depName=…' comment on the line above, such as the mise version that reads each repo's mise.lock.

packageRules.description: Patches that pass CI merge themselves on the weekly run. Renovate merges (not GitHub's auto-merge), so a red or missing check stops it.
Major versions: one PR each, always reviewed.

The windows-rs crates (windows, windows-core, windows-implement, …) come out on separate version lines, and a newer windows-core can't build with an older windows. They get their own PR that never merges itself, so a mismatch can't hold up the other crates; close it and Renovate skips that version.
GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs (a moved tag can't change what runs); the pin, digest, minor and patch updates come as one PR.
The Go toolchain in mise.toml and the Dockerfile's builder image move together.
Node in mise.toml and the Dockerfile's builder image move together.
The Rust toolchain in mise.toml and the Dockerfile's builder image move together.
mise itself (pinned in workflows) moves with the mise tools; mise.lock's format needs a recent mise.
